Prevention: Cut grass weeds from bordering fields.
Remove weeds regularly to reduce breeding sites and shelter for armyworm.
Conserve natural enemies – Lacewings, predatory wasps, parasitic wasps, flies, and spiders attack armyworm caterpillars, by less spraying of pesticides.
Monitoring: Regular monitoring to look in field margins, low areas where plants have lodged, beneath plant debris around the base of plants, on the ground, and underneath the plant leaves for egg masses or larva.
Monitor in late evening or early morning for adult moth as well.
Direct Control: Use botanical pesticide (e.g. fresh neem, lemongrass, ginger) 1 litre/15 litres of water.
This method is helpful, when caterpillars are found to be moving towards your field from the adjacent fields.
